title: 2027 Medicare final rules, explained for revenue cycle teams
summary: The 2027 physician fee schedule and OPPS final rules lower the conversion factor, cut same-day E/M payment, replace G2211 with modifier B1 and launch the Ambulatory Specialty Model. Here is what to change in your billing workflows.
body_markdown:
CMS released the calendar year 2027 Medicare Physician Fee Schedule (MPFS) and Hospital Outpatient Prospective Payment System (OPPS) final rules on November 4, 2026. Most provisions take effect January 1, 2027.


Some proposals were scaled back after public comment. Others passed as written. Either way, every practice billing Medicare has rates, codes and claim rules to update before the first 2027 claim goes out.


## At a glance


Change Proposed Final Effective


Conversion factor (non-QP) $32.84 $32.63, down 2.31% Jan 1, 2027


Same-day E/M with a procedure Lower service at 50%, 0-, 10- and 90-day globals Lower service at 80%, 0-day globals only, same specialty Jan 1, 2027


G2211 complexity add-on Replace with a modifier Modifier B1, +16% to the E/M payment Jan 1, 2027


RPM/RTM staffing Employed clinical staff only Delayed two years Jan 1, 2029


340B drugs in OPPS ASP minus 33.4% ASP minus 28% Jan 1, 2027


Site-neutral imaging Expand to imaging Finalized, imaging without contrast Jan 1, 2027


## The conversion factor drops about 2%


The one-year 2.5% increase Congress provided for 2026 expires. Statutory updates of 0.25% and 0.75% offset only part of it.


- **Clinicians who are not qualifying APM participants:** $32.63, down 2.31% from $33.40
- **Qualifying APM participants:** $32.95, down 1.83% from $33.57


Both cuts are deeper than CMS projected in July.


**What to update:** Load 2027 rates into your expected reimbursement tables. If those tables still hold 2026 rates, correctly paid Medicare claims will flag as short, and your team will spend January chasing underpayments that are not there.


## Same-day E/M visits with 0-day procedures are paid at 80%


CMS proposed paying the lower-valued service at 50% whenever a separately identifiable E/M visit fell on the same day as a 0-, 10- or 90-day global procedure. The final policy is narrower:


- It applies only to office and outpatient E/M visits billed with modifier 25 on the same day as a **0-day** global procedure
- The higher-paid service is paid in full and the other at **80%**
- It applies when the same physician, or a physician of the same specialty in the same group, furnishes both services. Same-day visits with a different specialty in the group are not reduced.


CMS expects[dermatology](https://www.embercopilot.ai/specialties/dermatology) ,[otolaryngology](https://www.embercopilot.ai/specialties/ent) and[podiatry](https://www.embercopilot.ai/specialties/podiatry) to see the largest effect.


**What to update:** Flag 0-day procedures in your charge rules and set expected payment at 80% for the lower-paid service, so a correctly reduced claim is not worked as a denial. Because specialty now decides whether the cut applies, check that each provider's specialty is accurate in Medicare enrollment and on claims.


## G2211 becomes modifier B1


The E/M complexity add-on code G2211 goes away in 2027. In its place:


- **Modifier B1** is appended to the E/M base code and raises its payment by 16%, instead of a flat add-on amount
- **Modifier B2** is for clinicians in a Medicare Shared Savings Program ACO or the LEAD Model, and raises the visit payment by 32%


CMS expects little change in total payment, since the volume billed under G2211 moves to the modifier. The bigger change is operational. As the American College of Cardiology pointed out, the extra payment no longer comes with its own RVUs, which complicates compensation models that credit work RVUs.


**What to update:** Remove G2211 from charge capture, templates and claim edits for dates of service on or after January 1, 2027. Add B1, or B2 for eligible ACO clinicians, and check that compensation reporting still credits the work.


## The Ambulatory Specialty Model starts January 1


The mandatory[Ambulatory Specialty Model](https://www.cms.gov/priorities/innovation/innovation-models/asm) (ASM) begins its first performance year on January 1, 2027, after CMS declined requests to delay it. It covers selected specialists in about a quarter of U.S. metro areas:


- **Heart failure cohort:**[cardiology](https://www.embercopilot.ai/specialties/cardiology)
- **Low back pain cohort:**[anesthesiology](https://www.embercopilot.ai/specialties/anesthesiology) ,[pain management](https://www.embercopilot.ai/specialties/pain-management) , neurosurgery,[orthopedic surgery](https://www.embercopilot.ai/specialties/orthopedics) and physical medicine and rehabilitation


Performance in 2027 sets a Part B payment adjustment of up to plus or minus 9% in 2029. Participants are exempt from MIPS for model years and must report 2027 data by March 31, 2028.


**What to update:** Check whether your clinicians are on CMS's final participant list. If they are, make sure quality and cost data are captured from the first visit of 2027, not reconstructed in 2028.


## Remote monitoring gets new requirements now, and a staffing rule in 2029


For 2027, CMS finalized three RPM and RTM changes as proposed:


- RTM can be furnished only to established patients
- Practices must furnish a separately reportable initiating visit when RPM or RTM begins
- CMS updated how these services are valued


The rule paying for RPM and RTM only when the practice's own employed clinical staff do the work, not contractors, was finalized with a two-year delay. It takes effect January 1, 2029.


**What to update:** Add an initiating visit check before RPM and RTM claims go out. If you use a third-party monitoring vendor, review that arrangement with your own counsel well before 2029.


## 340B and site-neutral pay: savings that stay in the hospital system


Two OPPS changes matter for independent practices mainly because of where the money goes.


- **340B drugs** move from ASP plus 6% to ASP minus 28%, based on CMS's drug acquisition cost survey. CMS had proposed ASP minus 33.4%.
- **Site-neutral payment** expands from drug administration, finalized last year, to certain imaging services without contrast at grandfathered off-campus hospital outpatient departments. Those services will be paid at 40% of the OPPS rate. Rural sole community hospitals are exempt.


In both cases the savings stay inside OPPS. CMS finalized an estimated 7.50% increase to other OPPS payments to offset the 340B cut, so practices paid under the physician fee schedule see no direct benefit. Redirecting those dollars would take an act of Congress.


## Other changes worth a look


- **OPPS and ASC rates** rise 2.3% for hospitals and ASCs that meet quality reporting requirements
- **Hospital outpatient prior authorization** expands to eight more botulinum toxin injection codes starting July 1, 2027
- **Medicare telehealth flexibilities** run through December 31, 2027
- **Advance care planning** by clinical staff under direct supervision moves to new codes G0572 and G0573, with CPT 99497 and 99498 reserved for the billing practitioner's own time
- **Traditional MIPS** ends with the 2031 performance period, giving clinicians through 2030 to move to MIPS Value Pathways or advanced APMs


## What to watch in Congress


- **[H.R. 4299](https://www.congress.gov/bill/119th-congress/house-bill/4299) , the Protecting Patient Access to Cancer and Complex Therapies Act.** Introduced by Rep. Greg Murphy in July 2025, the bill sits with the House Energy and Commerce and Ways and Means committees. Practices that administer Part B drugs should follow it.
- **Site neutrality and 340B.** So far CMS has expanded site-neutral pay through annual rulemaking, one service line at a time. Moving those savings, or the 340B savings, outside OPPS would take legislation, so watch for site-neutral bills in the next Congress.


## Your January 1 checklist


1. Load 2027 fee schedule rates into expected reimbursement and underpayment logic
2. Set 80% expected payment for the lower-paid service when a modifier 25 E/M falls on the same day as a 0-day procedure
3. Replace G2211 with modifier B1, or B2 for eligible ACO clinicians
4. Confirm each provider's specialty in Medicare enrollment and on claims
5. Check the ASM participant list and start capturing quality and cost data on day one
6. Add the RPM and RTM initiating visit check, and calendar your 2029 vendor review
7. Plan prior authorization for the added botulinum toxin codes before July 1


## Frequently asked questions


### When do the 2027 Medicare final rules take effect?


Most provisions apply to services on or after January 1, 2027. The RPM and RTM employed-staff rule takes effect January 1, 2029, and the added botulinum toxin prior authorization codes start July 1, 2027.


### What is the 2027 Medicare conversion factor?


$32.63 for clinicians who are not qualifying APM participants, down 2.31%, and $32.95 for qualifying APM participants, down 1.83%.


### What replaced G2211 in 2027?


Modifier B1, appended to the E/M code, which raises its payment by 16%. Clinicians in Shared Savings Program or LEAD Model ACOs can use modifier B2 for a 32% increase.


### Does the modifier 25 payment cut apply to 10- and 90-day global procedures?


No. The final rule applies the 80% payment only when an office or outpatient E/M visit falls on the same day as a 0-day global procedure, by the same physician or a same-specialty physician in the group.


### Can practices still use third-party vendors for RPM?


Yes, through 2028. Starting January 1, 2029, Medicare pays for RPM and RTM only when the practice's employed clinical staff perform the services.
